content.thinking:
I'm planning the postmortem and settling on the symptom: account pages failed for many shoppers. The causal chain starts with those failed account page requests, and I'll cite the two relevant incident references there. Next I'm tracing the cause to a ZeroDivisionError in the spend summary code.

I'm tracing the causal chain from the failed account page requests to a ZeroDivisionError in the spend summary code, and I'm checking whether the monthly-spend flag switch lines up with the onset. I'm also ruling out recent deploys, since the change window shows only that one flag change, and noting that ClientDisconnected errors were already present at baseline before the incident.

I'm working out the causal chain for the postmortem: the spend summary path divides by the number of purchases this month, which is empty for shoppers who only bought earlier, and that raises the ZeroDivisionError. I'm also checking whether the flag change and the ClientDisconnected errors that were already present before the onset affect that conclusion.

I'm settling the root cause: with the flag on, the monthly spend summary divides by this month's purchase count without a guard, so shoppers who bought earlier but not this month hit a ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47, and the account page turns that into a failed page.

I'm settling on the cause in plain terms: an admin switched on a new monthly spending summary for account pages, and its calculation then failed with a division by zero, most likely for shoppers who had bought before but nothing this month.

Next I'm settling the wording of the contributing factors, starting with the fact that the flag could be switched on for all production traffic at once.

I'm weighing whether the contributing factors need a check that would have stopped the flag from going on for all traffic at once, or switched it back when errors rose. A gradual rollout or automatic rollback would have limited how many shoppers were hit and how long it lasted. I'm also noting that no test was seen covering the monthly summary for a shopper with no purchases this month before the flag went on.

I'm thinking about the contributing factors now: the flag could be switched on for all production traffic at once, and I'm noting that no test was seen covering the monthly summary for a shopper with no purchases this month before the flag went on. I'm also looking at the account page boundary, which turned an error in an optional summary into a failed page instead of rendering the page without it.

I'm laying out the action items now, starting with preventing a recurrence of the contributing factor where the flag went on for all traffic at once: a gradual rollout by percentage of shoppers, watching the account-page error rate before widening. A separate item would have the flag switch back off automatically if errors rise after a change.

I'm drafting the postmortem's action items and lessons now, starting with the rollout guard for the flag, the test requirement for flag-gated code, and making the account page render without the spend summary when it fails.

I'm wrapping up the action items and lessons: the Mitigation Agent turned the flag off and confirmed the change, and the Code-Fix Agent proposed a draft PR. I'm now checking what went wrong and got lucky, and so far I'm not finding anything that fits either list.

I'm checking the causal chain's first step: shoppers' account pages failed to load, which the two incident references back up. The next step is that those failing requests raised a ZeroDivisionError in the spend summary code, starting in the minute the flag was switched on.

I'm now writing out the third causal step: the spend-summary path ran on account page requests because an admin switched the monthly-spend flag on, and the flag evaluations show it off right up to that minute, split during it, and on afterward. I'm also ruling out a deploy as the trigger, since the change window shows only that one flag change.

I'm checking that the ClientDisconnected errors were already present before the flag went on, and that the step naming the change stays free of Argus's later action and verdict. The fourth step is that with the flag on, the monthly spend summary divides by this month's purchase count, which is zero for shoppers who bought earlier but not this month.

action_items.item: Switch monthly-spend-feature, and other new feature flags, on in production gradually, for a growing share of shoppers, and widen it only while the error rate holds at its baseline.
Switch a feature flag back off automatically when the service's error rate rises soon after the flag is changed.
Require the test suite to pass with each new feature flag switched on before that flag can be switched on in production.
Make the account page render without the spend summary when computing the summary fails, instead of failing the whole page.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the logs report a rising account-page error rate.

The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError in the spend summary code (src/io_shop/spend_summary.py). This error first appears in the minute the onset is dated to and was not seen before it.

ruled_out.what: A deploy or release: none came back from the change window read, and the only production change read back was the flag switch.
Another flag change: the flag provider's history showed only one flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour read, the switch of monthly-spend-feature.
The ClientDisconnected account-page failures: they occurred throughout the half hour before the onset, while the flag was still off.

causal_chain.step: The spend summary code ran on account page requests because admin switched the monthly-spend-feature flag on at {P1.1}. The logs show the flag evaluated off in every minute before that, split between off and on during that minute, and on in every minute after.
With the flag on, the monthly spend summary divided by the number of the shopper's purchases this month, which is zero for a shopper who has bought before but not this month.

input.cause_in_plain_words: An admin switched on a new monthly spending summary for shoppers' account pages, and its calculation then failed with a division by zero, most likely for shoppers who had bought before but nothing yet this month, so their account pages failed to load.

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen that would have limited the monthly-spend-feature flag to a small share of shoppers when it was first switched on, or watched errors as it went out. Within a minute it was on for all traffic.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of shoppers' account pages would have failed, and the rise in errors could have stopped the rollout before it reached everyone.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No test was seen that ran the monthly spend summary for a shopper with no purchases this month before the flag was switched on in production. Code-Fix's reading says its new tests for that case would fail against the current code.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero would have been found before the flag was switched on, and the flag would not have been switched on with the fault in place.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: Code-Fix's reading of src/io_shop/account_page.py says the page's error boundary turned each error from the spend summary into a failed page. Nothing was seen that would render the page without the summary when the summary fails.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Account pages would have loaded without the spend summary rather than failing.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent formed a single candidate cause that tied the division-by-zero errors to the switch of the monthly-spend-feature flag, after reading the metrics, the change events and the logs.
The Mitigation Agent switched the monthly-spend-feature flag back off, a change that can be undone.
The Mitigation Agent checked the service after the revert, found it no longer at the incident's level, and confirmed the action.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request, PR #579, for a person to review.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, account page requests reach `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. It integer-divides the month's spend total by the number of purchases marked as this month, and nothing guards against that list being empty. A shopper who has bought before but not this month therefore raises ZeroDivisionError, and the boundary in src/io_shop/account_page.py turns that error into a failed page.
input.still_at_risk: Switching the monthly-spend-feature flag back on would likely make account pages fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month.
input.symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
